title: A quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces satisfying the existence part of the valuative criterion is universally closed
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: quasi-compactness together with the existence part of the valuative criterion forces a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a scheme S to be universally closed (source lines 8797-8807). After reducing to Y affine and to the closedness of |X| -> |Y|, the proof replaces an arbitrary closed T contained in |X| by the preimage of a closed subscheme Z of an affine etale cover U, reduces closedness to stability under specialization, and then runs the valuative argument: a specialization y' ~> y with y' in f(T) gives a point x' represented by Spec(K) -> X and a diagram with Spec(O_{Y,y}), a valuation ring A contained in K dominating the image of O_{Y,y} (possible because y' differs from y), and the assumed criterion produces K'/K and A' dominating A with Spec(A') -> X; the closed point of Spec(A') then maps to a point x of T specializing to x' with f(x) = y. Both the reduction to the affine case and the specialization argument are essential.
